questions.question: Prove that the opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary, and state the exterior-angle corollary with its one-line justification.
questions.expected_answer: Let ABCD be a cyclic quadrilateral with centre O. The inscribed angle at B stands on arc ADC, so the central angle on that arc equals 2B (angle at centre is twice angle at circumference). The inscribed angle at D stands on the remaining arc ABC, so its central angle equals 2D. These two central angles together complete a full revolution about O: 2B + 2D = 360°, hence B + D = 180°. The same argument applied to the other pair gives A + C = 180°. Corollary: extending DC beyond C to E, angle BCE = 180° − angle BCD because they lie on a straight line; but angle BAD = 180° − angle BCD by the theorem just proved; therefore the exterior angle BCE equals the interior opposite angle BAD.

questions.question: Prove that two tangents drawn to a circle from the same external point are equal, naming the axiom and the congruency condition used.
questions.expected_answer: Let the tangents from external point P touch the circle with centre O at A and B. Join OA, OB and OP. The angles OAP and OBP are each 90° because a tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact (the CAPS axiom, quoted as tangent perpendicular to radius). In triangles OAP and OBP: OA = OB (radii), OP is common and is the hypotenuse of both right-angled triangles. By the right angle, hypotenuse, side condition the triangles are congruent, so PA = PB. The tangents are equal, quoted in riders as tangents from same point. A consequence worth noting: triangle PAB is isosceles, so the base angles PAB and PBA are equal.

questions.question: PA and PB are tangents from P touching a circle at A and B, with angle APB = 40°, and C lies on the major arc AB. Find angle ACB by the tangent-chord route, then confirm it through the centre.
questions.expected_answer: Route one: PA = PB (tangents from same point), so triangle PAB is isosceles and angles PAB = PBA = (180° − 40°) ÷ 2 = 70° (base angles of isosceles triangle; angle sum). Angle PAB is the angle between tangent PA and chord AB, so the angle subtended by AB in the alternate segment equals 70°: angle ACB = 70° (tangent-chord). Route two: in quadrilateral OAPB the angles at A and B are each 90° (tangent perpendicular to radius), so angle AOB = 360° − 90° − 90° − 40° = 140° (angle sum of quadrilateral). The circumference angle on the major arc is half the central angle: angle ACB = 70° (angle at centre). Both roads give 70°, confirming the answer.
